source: RH-Alpoge-Reconstruction manuscript/sec5_auxiliary.tex (C9), source explicitly applies h=1 with logQ<=10*(logX)^(2/5) and X=(kb)^8.
needed: Only the DYADIC count for X<g<=2X under logQ<=10*(logX)^(2/5) is used; the separately stated uniformity for all h as small as exp(-c sqrt(logX)) is not needed for that application.
conditionalFromC9: Assuming C9, count>=cPrime*X/(Q^A logX). Let y=log X. It exceeds X^(9/10) whenever y/10 >= 10A y^(2/5)+log y-log cPrime. For any fixed A,cPrime>0 this holds for sufficiently large y. Moreover logQ<=10 y^(2/5) implies logQ<=c sqrt y once y >=(10/c)^10. These are elementary comparisons; this file does not prove C9 itself.
caveat: Uniform count in varying imaginary quadratic ray class fields including possible exceptional real zero is the source theorem not sourced in the human manuscript. We found no directly source-matching peer-reviewed statement in this pass. A dyadic-only theorem plus Siegel/zero-free/density estimates could be a substantially smaller proof target. The numerical roots are illustrative, not universal bound without actual constants.
